items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1965-09-13
items.q: I'll put it the way Nick LaRocca put it... Nick LaRocca always said this

ctx.x: I think this brings to mind something else. It's kind of a confused tradition in New Orleans that's been brought up that the glorification of the older musicians by critics and by fans has often overemphasized the older Negro musicians. I think we had some rabid white musicians who'd complain about this like Nick Garaka in kind of extreme terms and it's been sort of a cluttered image that's been presented to the public. You as a person who understudied the earlier jazz musicians, colored and white, might be able…

Well, I'll put it the way Nick LaRocca put it, as you say. I think that the jazz music belongs to New Orleans. You hate to get into something where you say which was better, was the colored music better or the white jazz music better? I think that stuff stuff

music had its place where they had the marching bands, which was a definite, a particular style of New Orleans, which I think belonged entirely, mostly, to the to the to the colored people. However, I do believe this, that the white musicians brought jazz to a higher level, to a higher standard, in when they brought it to New York. For instance, Nick LaRocca always said this, that that when they went to New York with their band, they played a different type of jazz. In fact, if you listen to it, if you listen to…
